tagline: Short essays on design, work, and everyday life.

posts.title: Slow Mornings
posts.excerpt: Why the first hour of the day deserves more margin than the rest.
posts.author: Mihyun
posts.body:
I used to treat mornings as a race to inbox zero. The shift came when I blocked thirty minutes with no inputs—no feeds, no messages, just coffee and a notebook.

That small buffer changed how the rest of the day felt. Decisions arrived with less noise. Writing came easier because the first words were mine, not borrowed urgency.

If you are building a minimal site, protect one ritual the way you protect a logo: same time, same place, same silence.

posts.title: One Typeface Is Enough
posts.excerpt: Consistency beats variety when readability is the goal.
posts.author: Mihyun
posts.body:
Every new font in a project is a relationship to maintain. Families, weights, fallbacks, and licensing multiply quickly.

For editorial layouts, a single family with clear hierarchy—display size for titles, text size for body—often outperforms a pairing chosen for novelty.

Let color and spacing carry personality instead.

posts.title: Lists Over Grids for Blogs
posts.excerpt: Vertical rhythm helps readers scan without visual competition.
posts.author: Mihyun
posts.body:
Card grids look rich in marketing demos and tired in daily reading. A simple list—date, title, one-line summary—respects attention.

Thumbnails are optional. When they appear, keep them small so the title remains the anchor.

posts.title: Draft in Public, Publish in Private
posts.author: Mihyun
posts.body:
Social posts are sketches. Blog posts are rooms you invite people into. The difference is editing and intent.

Write messy notes elsewhere. Publish when a single idea can stand without footnotes.

posts.title: The Footer as a Closing Sentence
posts.excerpt: End pages with calm, not clutter.
posts.author: Mihyun
posts.body:
Footers accumulate links like attics accumulate boxes. For minimal templates, one copyright line and maybe a single social link is enough.

Everything else can live on About.

posts.title: CMS as Master Slide
posts.excerpt: One post layout, many URLs—like a template that repeats.
posts.author: Mihyun
posts.body:
In Wix, dynamic item pages behave like PowerPoint masters: design once, populate with collection data.

Static pages handle Home and About. The list page handles discovery. The item page handles depth.

posts.title: Feature Only One Post
posts.excerpt: A single highlight on Home beats a carousel.
posts.author: Mihyun
posts.body:
Home should answer two questions: what is this site, and what should I read first?

Mark one post as featured and show three or four recent titles beneath. That is sufficient hierarchy.

posts.title: Keep About Static
posts.excerpt: Bio pages change rarely; posts change often.
posts.author: Mihyun
posts.body:
Resist turning About into another feed. A portrait, two paragraphs, and a link back to the blog is a complete page.

Save CMS connections for content that actually repeats.
